# Senior Walk In Tub

> Walk-in tub guidance written for the older adult who will use the tub: how your step, standing up, hips and knees, walker or wheelchair, and body size decide which tub type fits. Published by Aging Safely Baths & More (Aging Safely Baths), a walk-in tub and roll-in shower supplier and installer serving all 50 U.S. states, with supply-only delivery to Canada. Phone 1-888-779-2284, email sales@agingsafelybaths.com. BBB accredited.

This site covers body fit and self-checks for seniors choosing a tub for themselves. Family and caregiver decisions are on walkintubsforelderly.com; hydrotherapy and jets are on walkintubswithjets.com; national costs, Medicare, VA, tax rules, sizes and the full model lineup are on agingsafelybaths.com.

## Tools and guides
- [Walk-In Tub Fit Check for Seniors](https://seniorwalkintub.com/walk-in-tub-fit-check/): A nine-question self-check (step-in, standing up, hip or knee replacement, bending limits, cane/walker/wheelchair, build, bathing style, space, help) that points to a tub type: standard seated, compact, wide or bariatric, lay-down, wheelchair transfer, or a roll-in shower instead. Runs in the browser; nothing is sent.
- [Walk-In Tub After Hip or Knee Replacement](https://seniorwalkintub.com/walk-in-tub-after-hip-or-knee-replacement/): What MedlinePlus, the AAOS, Hospital for Special Surgery and Alberta Health Services say about tub transfers, seat height and soaking after joint replacement, a recovery-stage table, and a seat-height checker.
- [Getting In and Out of a Walk-In Tub With Arthritis or Balance Problems](https://seniorwalkintub.com/getting-in-and-out-of-a-walk-in-tub/): The four risky moments of a walk-in tub bath, step-by-step entry and exit routines, the features that help, and a home self-check. Based on CDC STEADI, CDC MMWR, ADA and CPSC sources.
- [Walk-In Tub With Diabetes or Neuropathy](https://seniorwalkintub.com/walk-in-tub-diabetes-neuropathy/): Bathing safely when neuropathy blunts heat sensation in the feet: NIDDK foot-care guidance, CPSC scald times and the 120°F heater setting, anti-scald valves, a seated bath routine, and questions for a doctor or podiatrist.
- [Living Alone With a Walk-In Tub](https://seniorwalkintub.com/living-alone-walk-in-tub-safety/): A solo bathing plan: why the door stays sealed until the tub drains, quick drains, alert pendants and other ways to call for help from the seat, door choices, and when a shower suits someone living alone better.

## Main pages
- [Senior Walk In Tub](https://seniorwalkintub.com/): Overview of senior walk-in tubs: safety features, one-day installation or DIY delivery, VA HISA information and FAQs.

## Key facts (checked 2026-10-22; last two added 2026-10-25)
- ADA 2010 Standards section 610.2: bathtub seats 17 to 19 inches above the finished floor (https://www.access-board.gov/ada/#ada-610). Private homes are not required to comply; the range is a reference point.
- AAOS OrthoInfo suggests an 18 to 20 inch chair with a firm seat and two arms during early knee replacement recovery, and grab bars, a shower bench and a raised toilet seat at home (https://www.orthoinfo.org/en/treatment/total-knee-replacement/).
- MedlinePlus (hip replacement): keep hips higher than knees when sitting, avoid hip flexion past 90 degrees, and do not sit in the bottom of a regular bathtub (https://medlineplus.gov/ency/patientinstructions/000171.htm).
- CDC STEADI Stay Independent brochure: needing to push with your hands to stand from a chair and trouble stepping onto a curb are signs of weak leg muscles; 4 or more points suggests fall risk.
- CDC MMWR 2011 (2008 data, age 15+): 81.1% of bathroom injuries treated in emergency departments were caused by falls; 68.3% happened in or near the tub or shower.
- NIDDK: up to one-half of people with diabetes have peripheral neuropathy, which can cause problems sensing temperature in the feet; NIDDK advises testing wash water with a thermometer (90 to 95°F) or the elbow (https://www.niddk.nih.gov/health-information/diabetes/overview/preventing-problems/foot-problems).
- ACL 2023 Profile of Older Americans: about 28% of community-dwelling adults 65+ lived alone (https://acl.gov/news-and-events/announcements/acl-releases-2023-profile-older-americans).

## Safety language
No bathing product removes the risk of a fall. This site gives general information, not medical advice; readers with a joint replacement or recent fall should follow their surgeon's or therapist's instructions.
